questions.prompt: What money is used in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Bosnia and Herzegovina is the convertible mark.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Sarajevo?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Bosnia and Herzegovina is Sarajevo.

questions.prompt: Which continent is Bosnia and Herzegovina in?

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Bosnia and Herzegovina on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Bosnia and Herzegovina on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.proof: Bosnia and Herzegovina is in Europe.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Bosnia and Herzegovina about 51,209 square kilometres; North Macedonia about 25,713 square kilometres; Montenegro about 13,883 square kilometres; Kosovo about 10,909 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bosnia and Herzegovina article.

questions.proof: The capital is Sarajevo, and other important cities are Banja Luka, Mostar, Bihać, Zenica and Tuzla.
